intended_object: The restriction of a total function f : α → β to a subset s ⊆ α, seen as a partial function. Its domain is exactly s, and it takes the value f a at each a ∈ s. This reading comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The definition lifts f to a total partial function, `PFun.lift f`, whose domain is all of α. It then restricts that lift to s with `PFun.restrict`, which gives the partial function x ↦ (f x).restrict (x ∈ s). The lemma `mem_res` in the same file confirms that b ∈ res f s a holds exactly when a ∈ s and f a = b, so the domain is s and the values are those of f. The construction works for arbitrary types α and β, so it is at its natural generality. This is the standard notion of the restriction of a function to a subset, expressed as a partial function. There is no separate Mathlib definition of the same object; this definition is itself part of Mathlib.
